title: Arriving in Oliver's band and how it differed from New Orleans
summary: Armstrong recalls feeling not good enough at the door, the band's setup versus New Orleans, the repertoire, and going straight to work as second cornet with no rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The End The End When I went at the door I said, I ain't good enough for this band, I think I'll go back. Yeah, that's the highlight of, you know, my biggest moments.
Well, was this a different kind of a band than bands that you had played with in New Orleans?

Well, it was the same setup, but see we didn't have no pianos in New Orleans, no guitars. No one was on the piano here, see what I mean? Was he using two cornets before you came up? No, just by himself. And I don't know, the band was wailing.
I fit right in there sitting with Joe because I admired him so anyway, you know. Well, when you first came in to hear the band, were they playing tunes that you knew?

Well, the usual Dixieland numbers in New Orleans because there was others that I didn't know, like these. They would come up later who wrote these. But we played the usual Panama and the things that we did in New Orleans, you know. With the blues and things like that.

Now before you started in with a band like that, with Joe's band, when you got to Chicago, did you have to rehearse with them? No, I just went to work. Just went to work with them? Yeah, it was a while.
Wow. But I knew all the boys. Yeah. And then they would do routine, you know. And I'd just sit in there and went to work the next night. And I played second jumping to everything he played. Uh-huh.
